frozen_question: Could the textual Mendes metal female matrix or phallus/spine relic container already exist in excavation or museum records under generic labels such as vessel, sheath, case, socket, fitting, bronze/copper object, gold fitting, reliquary or unidentified cult object?

method_execution.TOPA_SPIDER: Search Mendes/Tell el-Rub'a excavation bibliography, museum provenance trails and object catalogues using target and generic material-object vocabulary.
method_execution.FIVE_D_SPIRAL: findspot -> date -> material -> morphology -> cult association -> inventory identity -> contradiction return
method_execution.BEETLE_GRAZER: Deduplicate modern object pages that descend from the same excavation/catalogue record; absence in one museum index is not counted as independent negative evidence.
method_execution.TENET_REVERSE: Trace textual predicted object classes backward into old excavation language without requiring excavators to have recognized Osirian anatomy.

nesbanebdjedet_tomb.discovery: 1902, Egyptian Antiquities Service / Aly Habib; reported by J. E. Quibell
nesbanebdjedet_tomb.occupant: Nesbanebdjedet, priest connected with the Banebdjedet cult
nesbanebdjedet_tomb.inventory_summary: More than 360 complete shabtis plus fragments and several amulets were recorded on/around the burial; beneath them was the mummy with gold-leaf trappings. Metropolitan Museum documentation points to Cairo CG 53465-53469 for related burial equipment.

cg53465_53469_control.group_link: Metropolitan Museum documentation connects the Nesbanebdjedet burial to Cairo CG 53465-53469.
cg53465_53469_control.boundary: Earlier JANUS descriptions of CG 53469 must not be promoted here until the original catalogue entry, plate or museum record is recovered.

inventory_result.interpretation: The current negative result means no target object was identified in accessible records searched; it does not establish that the object never existed, was destroyed, hidden, removed, or remains uncatalogued.
